correctness.rationale: The digit functions h_j are orthogonal and centered under Lebesgue measure. The observable transition operator gives P h_0=p h_1 and P h_j=p h_(j+1)+(1-p)h_(j-1) (j>=1). Its zero-to-zero 2m paths are Dyck excursions, each weighted [p(1-p)]^m, explaining C_m. Pair counting yields exact finite variance; Catalan series sums to 1/max(p,1-p), with unique neutral maximum at p=1/2. Stirling C_m/4^m=(pi m^3)^(-1/2)+O(m^-5/2) gives the sqrt(N) deficit coefficient 8 sqrt(2N/pi); differentiating the Catalan series gives the offcritical intercept. Independently propagated finite-digit stochastic operator for 25 parameter/lag checks; finite check not proof.

value.rationale: One-time stationary marginals are parameter-independent, making parameter-sensitive temporal covariance a natural and nontrivial observable. The precise Catalan law, sharp maximum at the zero-Lyapunov transition and distinct finite-size corrections give a complete temporal classification, not just isolated finite simulations.

final_claim: For iid random base-b expansion (p) or uniformly chosen inverse branch (1-p), uniform stationary initial law, and nonconstant centered leading-digit f, lag-2m covariance is sigma_f² C_m[p(1-p)]^m and odd covariances vanish; finite and asymptotic integrated variance formulas with unique p=1/2 maximum and critical sqrt(N) correction.
limitations: Annealed stationary uniform X0, balanced inverse-branch selection and leading-digit observables only.
No quenched or higher digit result or central limit theorem.
